2: The software requirements document and SRS standards
3: Cyclomatic Complexity Measures: Control Flow Graphs

questions.q: True or False: Adding more programmers to a software project that is already late will reliably make it finish sooner.
questions.model: False. New people need training and add communication paths (Brooks' law), which usually delays a late project further.

questions.q: Why is the spiral model called risk-driven? Describe the four activities of each loop of the spiral.
questions.model: Each loop starts by identifying and resolving the main risks before committing further. Activities: determine objectives and constraints; identify and resolve risks (e.g. prototypes); develop and verify the next-level product; plan the next iteration with customer review.

questions.q: Read the assertion and reason about the agile development process and choose the correct option.
questions.assertion: Agile methods deliver working software in short iterations and adapt to changing requirements.
questions.reason: Agile methods value comprehensive documentation over working software.
questions.model: A is true; R is false: the Agile Manifesto values working software over comprehensive documentation.

questions.q: Recommend a software development life-cycle model for each project in the case and justify each choice against the alternatives.
questions.case: (1) Payroll software for a firm with stable, well-understood rules and a fixed deadline. (2) A first-of-its-kind student mental-health app whose users cannot describe their needs precisely. (3) A large defence communication system with high technical risk and a multi-year budget.
questions.model: (1) Waterfall (or incremental): requirements are stable and well documented. (2) Prototyping or agile: user feedback on early versions clarifies needs. (3) Spiral: explicit risk analysis each cycle suits high-risk, large, long projects. Waterfall would be risky for (2) and (3); spiral is too heavy for (1).

questions.q: Which of the following is a non-functional requirement for an online examination portal?
opts: The system shall let a teacher submit a question for review
The system shall generate a question paper from a blueprint
The system shall respond to 95% of requests within 2 seconds
The system shall let a reviewer approve a question
questions.model: Response time is a performance (quality) requirement; the others describe functions.

questions.q: A library allows borrowing if the member has no overdue books and has fewer than 5 books issued; a member with overdue books is fined, and a member who already has 5 books is told the limit is reached. Draw a decision table with conditions, actions and rules.
questions.model: Conditions: C1 overdue books? C2 books issued < 5? Rules: (N, Y) -> issue book; (N, N) -> limit reached; (Y, Y) -> fine, do not issue; (Y, N) -> fine and limit reached, do not issue.

questions.q: Draw (describe) the context-level (level 0) DFD for a library management system and give two data dictionary entries for its data flows.
questions.model: One process 'Library Management System'; external entities Member, Librarian; flows: borrow request, return details, issue slip, fine notice, reports. Data dictionary: borrow request = member_id + book_id + date; issue slip = member_id + book_id + due_date.

questions.t: The software requirements document and SRS standards
questions.q: Prepare the outline of an SRS document, following the IEEE 830 structure, for a hostel room-allocation system, with one example requirement in each requirements section.
questions.model: 1 Introduction (purpose, scope, definitions, references, overview); 2 Overall description (product perspective, functions, user classes, constraints, assumptions); 3 Specific requirements: functional (e.g. 'The system shall allocate a room by merit rank'), external interfaces, performance ('allocation results within 5 s'), design constraints, attributes (security: only wardens edit allocations).

questions.q: Which combination characterises a good modular design?
questions.model: Modules should be independent (low coupling) and focused (high cohesion).

questions.t: Cyclomatic Complexity Measures: Control Flow Graphs
questions.q: A function's control flow graph has 9 edges and 7 nodes and is a single connected component. What is its cyclomatic complexity?
questions.model: V(G) = E - N + 2 = 9 - 7 + 2 = 4: four independent paths to test.

questions.q: A system has 5 external inputs, 4 external outputs, 3 external inquiries, 2 internal logical files and 1 external interface file, all of average complexity (weights 4, 5, 4, 10, 7). The 14 general system characteristics total 42. Compute the function points.
State the intent of the Singleton and Observer design patterns and give one situation in an exam portal where each would be appropriate.
questions.model: Singleton: exactly one instance with a global access point (e.g. the configuration or connection-pool manager). Observer: dependents are notified when a subject changes (e.g. notify reviewers when a question is submitted).

questions.q: Compare white-box and black-box testing in terms of what they are based on, who typically performs them, and the kinds of defects each is better at finding.
questions.model: White-box is based on code structure (statement, branch, path coverage), done by developers; finds untested paths and logic errors. Black-box is based on specifications (equivalence classes, boundaries), done by testers; finds missing or incorrect functions and interface errors.

questions.q: In top-down integration testing, lower-level modules that are not yet developed are replaced by:
questions.model: Stubs stand in for called modules; drivers stand in for callers (bottom-up).

questions.q: An applicant's age must be from 18 to 60 inclusive. Design test cases using equivalence partitioning and boundary value analysis.
questions.model: Partitions: below 18 (invalid), 18-60 (valid), above 60 (invalid): e.g. 10, 35, 70. Boundaries: 17, 18, 19, 59, 60, 61.

questions.q: True or False: Regression testing re-runs previously passed tests after a change to check that existing functionality still works.
questions.model: True; it guards against new defects introduced by changes.

questions.q: Using basic COCOMO for an organic project (E = 2.4 x KLOC^1.05 person-months), estimate the effort for a 32 KLOC project. Give two decimal places.
Changing a released system to fix a defect reported by its users is which category of maintenance?
questions.model: Fixing reported faults is corrective maintenance.

questions.q: Risk R1 has probability 0.3 and would cost Rs 5 lakh; risk R2 has probability 0.6 and would cost Rs 2 lakh. Compute each risk exposure, decide which to address first, and propose one mitigation for it.
questions.model: RE = probability x loss: R1 = 1.5 lakh, R2 = 1.2 lakh. Address R1 first (higher exposure). Mitigation depends on the risk, e.g. for a key-staff loss risk: cross-training and documentation; monitor both risks.

questions.q: List the five maturity levels of the SEI Capability Maturity Model in order.
questions.model: Initial, Repeatable, Defined, Managed, Optimizing.
